1. Inspect the brake system: Conduct a thorough examination of the brake system components, including pads, rotors, calipers, and brake lines. Document any visible signs of wear or damage.

2. Check the brake fluid level: Check the brake fluid reservoir and note the fluid level and condition. If the fluid level is low or the fluid appears dirty, this could be an indication of a brake system leak or other issues.

3. Test the brake pedal: Depress the brake pedal several times to check for spongy or soft feel. If the pedal feels spongy or if the vehicle takes longer to stop than usual, this could indicate a brake system issue.

4. Perform a road test: Take the vehicle for a test drive and evaluate the performance of the brakes. Check for any pulling or vibrating when applying the brakes.

5. Record the test results
